# Flow: background refresh (Rebuild snapshot / Read Snowflake again)

One-line summary: a refresh reads every part again under a key of its own, builds it, and only then swaps it in; the pages keep answering from the data they have, and a failure keeps it (`server.py:2371-2421`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor U as User
    participant W as React App.tsx
    participant S as server.py
    participant C as cache.py
    participant SF as Snowflake
    U->>W: Read Snowflake again / Rebuild snapshot
    W->>S: POST /api/reload {what: page | rebuild}
    S->>S: reload -> refresh(what): JOB {id, state: running}
    S-->>W: {ok, started, job} (BACKGROUND) — the thread goes on
    S->>SF: renew: CALL SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT('AUTO') (rebuild, objects mode)
    S->>C: clear_parts(KEY.new) when its parts are over an hour old; read_shared(KEY.new)
    S->>S: built(d): build + rule checks
    S->>C: swap(KEY, KEY.new, d): parts folder replaced, store()
    loop once a second
        W->>S: GET /api/progress
        S-->>W: {running, lines, job}
    end
    W->>W: job done / failed: clearCache, notice; the pages fetch the new data
```

## Steps

1. `reload(body)`: a `--build` run refuses all but `load` (`BUILD_ONLY_NOTE`); `load` is the Direct-mode click (`load_shared()`); fake mode drops the copy; else `refresh(what)` — `server.py:2354-2368`.
2. `refresh(what)`: one `JOB` at a time (a second answers "A refresh is already running") — `server.py:2374-2379`; `job()` runs `renew()` and records `done` / `failed`, `ok`, `message` — `server.py:2381-2388`. `BACKGROUND` (not inside Snowflake, `server.py:63`) starts a daemon thread and answers `{ok, started, job}`; otherwise runs it inline — `server.py:2389-2398`.
3. `renew(what)` under `LOAD` and `tracked(KEY, "shared", ...)` — `server.py:2401-2421`: rebuild in objects mode CALLs `call_snapshot()` first; a status other than OK keeps the data and says "Snapshot skipped / failed: <error>" — `server.py:2407-2412`, `server.py:2424-2436`.
4. The read goes to `KEY + ".new"`: its parts are cleared first only when older than an hour, so a refresh that failed within the hour resumes; then `read_shared(new)`, `built(d)`, `cache.swap(KEY, new, d)` (its parts become the key's) — `server.py:2403`, `server.py:2413-2417`.
5. `cache.swap(key, new, d)` under `lock(key)`: key's parts folder removed, new's renamed into its place, then `store(key, d)` (memory, `.pkl` with the previous as `.prev.pkl`, SQL copy thread) — `cache.py:164-171`, `cache.py:144-161`.
6. `GET /api/progress` carries `job` (`server.py:136`); type `Progress.job` — `web/src/api/types.ts:169-170`.
7. React: `refresh(what)` posts the reload; `started` -> `bg` state with the job id and its message — `web/src/App.tsx:298-307`. While `bg` is set the top bar shows a spinner button "Reading again: <latest line>" / "Rebuilding: ..." that opens the full log — `web/src/App.tsx:376-381`, `web/src/App.tsx:403`; Rebuild and Read again are disabled meanwhile. A poll every second ends when `job.id` matches and its state is not running: `clearCache()`, a notice with the outcome; no job or another id means the server restarted during it: the indicator stops and says to click again — `web/src/App.tsx:309-337`.
8. Inside Snowflake `app.py` sets `server.BACKGROUND = False` (one call at a time; the refresh shows its lines as the first load does) and `server.LOG_LINES = True` — `app.py:10-11`.

## Related: the first load

- A page never waits behind a load: `load_shared` takes `LOAD` without blocking and answers 409 `shared_loading` — `server.py:185-186`. The React app then makes the page inert (`lock`), shows "The shared data is being read from Snowflake", polls `/api/progress` every 1.5 s and asks again when it ends — `web/src/App.tsx:348-355`, `web/src/App.tsx:422`.
- Before any data the SQL buttons, the `</>` note and right-click SQL are hidden (`hasData`) — `web/src/App.tsx:356`, `web/src/App.tsx:384-385`, `web/src/App.tsx:397`.

## Example

- test_server.test_background: during a refresh the pages answer at once from the old data; after it they show the new run; a failed read keeps the old data and `/api/progress` `job` says why — `test_server.py:867-912`.
- web/src/app.test.tsx: no SQL buttons before data, the first load locks the page; Read Snowflake again keeps it usable, the top bar shows the latest line, then the new data — `web/src/app.test.tsx:21-57`.

Rule: [business_rule:background_refresh](../logic/rules.md), [business_rule:page_never_waits](../logic/rules.md). Progress lines: [load-progress.md](load-progress.md).
